idiom_name: hand-written endpoint over a SwiftNIO MQTT client (MQTTNIO)
implementation_notes: Swift ships no messaging runtime, so the endpoint is assembled by hand over a client package: with mqtt-nio the endpoint is scoped inside MQTTConnection.withConnection { ... }, receives messages as an AsyncSequence returned by connection.subscribe(to:) { subscription in for try await message in subscription ... } and publishes via connection.publish(to:payload:qos:). Topic naming, payload codec, QoS/ack policy and reconnection are application responsibilities; the classic full structure stays justified because nothing in the standard library replaces it (an AMQP client such as the Bunny-style Swift port exists only as a community package).
pitfalls: Leaving the subscribe closure sends UNSUBSCRIBE and cleans the subscription up: keep the endpoint alive for exactly as long as messages are wanted.
The AsyncSequence loop processes one message at a time, so a slow handler back-pressures the subscription; fan work out explicitly if throughput matters.
Client packages are not part of the platform: pin the version, because API and reconnection behaviour of community MQTT/AMQP clients change between releases.
